description: Start an import from a CSV or Excel file: up to 10 MB and 50,000 rows. A CSV's cells are separated by commas, semicolons or tabs. An Excel file (.xlsx, .xlsm or .xls) is read from its first visible sheet only, as the text its cells show, and a formula as its last saved result. Send it as `content` (its bytes in base64), or a CSV as `csv` (text), with its `fileName`. A file we can't read (locked with a password, too much text, or another format such as Numbers or OpenDocument) answers 400 and says what to do: save the list as .xlsx or CSV. Nothing changes in your contacts yet: it answers the columns it found, the settings it suggests (the columns it recognized, `mode: skip`, a label named after the file) and `preview`, a dry run of what they would do. Change them with update_contact_import, then call commit_contact_import with the `revision` you read. On MCP a whole call is capped at 1 MB, about 750 KB of CSV: for a bigger file call create_contact_import_upload and PUT its bytes from a shell, use REST, or upsert_contacts 500 rows at a time. `csv` counts as UTF-8 bytes, and a file full of quotes can pass the request's limit first, because JSON escapes each one: send that file as `content`. A big file can take over a minute: wait up to 2 minutes for the answer. The SDK does this on its own. An import you don't commit is deleted, file and all, after 24 hours.

content.description: The file's bytes, in base64: a CSV or an Excel file (.xlsx, .xlsm or .xls). We read a CSV's encoding (UTF-8, UTF-16 or Windows-1252) from its bytes, and an Excel file's first visible sheet. The file can be up to 10 MB. On MCP a whole call is capped at 1 MB, so send about 750 KB of file at most there, use create_contact_import_upload for raw bytes from a shell, or use upsert_contacts 500 at a time.

csv.description: The file as text, when you already have it as text: up to 10 MB. Cells are separated by commas, semicolons or tabs. On MCP a whole call is capped at 1 MB.

fileName.description: The file's name, like leads.csv. It's shown back to you, and the import's label is named after it.

idempotencyKey.description: Your own id for this one call, such as a UUID, up to 255 characters. If the call fails with no answer, call again with the same key and the same arguments: within 24 hours, a saved answer comes back instead of a second run. A call left unanswered can run again after 15 minutes, so a send also keeps its intentKey or draft revision.

name: create_contact_import
title: Start a contact import
